drhp.business: Turtlemint is a tech-enabled insurance distribution platform that empowers a large network of Digital Partners (including PoSPs) to sell insurance and other financial products to customers. It adopted the PoSP distribution model in 2015 and operates a mobile-first advisor platform (Turtlemint Pro) plus enterprise offerings (Turtlefin, OneAPI). It acquired insurance broker TIB (Turtlemint Insurance Broking Services) in May 2024.

compliance_legal.detail: Has entered and will continue to enter related party transactions; may not achieve terms as favourable as with unrelated parties; potential conflicts of interest.
compliance_legal.title: Related party transactions

compliance_legal.detail: Governed by IRDAI, AMFI, FIU and other authorities; TIB holds composite broker registration with minimum capital and net-worth requirements; PoSP product caps limit product range; TIB received a 2020 advisory/show cause notice from IRDAI enforcement.
compliance_legal.evidence: Composite broker minimum paid-up capital Rs 50.00 million; net worth not below 50% of minimum capital; PoSP health indemnity sum-assured cap Rs 0.50 million; TIB 2020 show cause notice (no penalties levied)
compliance_legal.title: Stringent and evolving regulatory framework; compliance costs and penalties

compliance_legal.detail: TIB subject to IRDAI inspections; past inspections (Dec 2019) led to observations, advisory (July 2020), show cause notice (Aug 6, 2020) and IRDAI directive/caution (June 7, 2021); AMFI due diligence on TMF (report May 23, 2025) had no observations.
compliance_legal.evidence: IRDAI inspection Dec 16-20, 2019; show cause notice dated Aug 6, 2020; IRDAI order dated June 7, 2021 (no penalties); AMFI report on TMF dated May 23, 2025 (no observations/penalties)
compliance_legal.title: Periodic IRDAI and AMFI inspections and due diligence

compliance_legal.detail: Instances of delay in TDS, provident fund and ESIC payments; risk of penalties/fines; new third-party vendor appointed for compliance.
compliance_legal.evidence: Delays: TDS 0.14 instances/Rs 0.89m (FY2025); provident fund 1.06 instances/Rs 1.42m (FY2025), 8.98m (FY2024); ESIC 0.01/Rs 0.06m; unpaid dues Nil as at Dec 31, 2025 (PF dues paid Rs 85.50m, TDS Rs 166.24m)
compliance_legal.title: Past delays in payment of statutory dues

compliance_legal.detail: Pending tax, regulatory and criminal proceedings; TIB named in civil/consumer cases (as intermediary) and ex-employee wrongful-termination suits; no provision made for pending legal/tax matters.

financial_valuation.detail: Incurred restated losses and negative operating cash flows across all periods; net worth declined from March 31, 2023 to December 31, 2025; negative RONW and EPS throughout.
financial_valuation.title: History of losses, negative operating cash flows, declining net worth and negative EPS/RONW

financial_valuation.detail: Revenue derived from commissions/rewards/fees from Insurer Partners and other providers; EOM caps, GST exemption on individual life/health premiums (effective Sep 2025) and unilateral rate cuts could reduce commissions.
financial_valuation.evidence: Income from distribution of financial products = 98.91% and 96.96% of revenue in 9M Dec 2025/2024, and proforma 97.99%, 90.75%, 29.56% in FY2025/2024/2023; a general insurer cut motor commission from 32.50% (Aug 1, 2023) to 30.00% (Aug 1, 2024); industry commission payouts rose ~97% from Rs 201.4bn (FY2023) to Rs 396.0bn (FY2024) per Redseer
financial_valuation.title: Almost all revenue from commissions, rewards and fees; fee-rate reduction risk

financial_valuation.detail: TIB acquired May 8, 2024 from Promoter Dhirendra Nalin Mahyavanshi; group lacks long consolidated history; Unaudited Proforma Financial Information illustrative, not GAAP-prepared, may not reflect future results.
financial_valuation.evidence: TIB Acquisition effective May 8, 2024; buyback dated Sep 21, 2024; proforma as if consummated Apr 1, 2024/2023/2022
financial_valuation.title: TIB acquisition: no long consolidated operating history; proforma info illustrative only

financial_valuation.detail: Regulatory changes (FY2024) ended marketing fees as a major revenue source while TIB acquisition made distribution income dominant, making periods non-comparable.
financial_valuation.evidence: Income from marketing fees = 53.62% and 88.05% of revenue in FY2024/2023; income from distribution of financial products = 8.83% and 0.58% (FY2024/2023) rising to 97.63%/98.91%/96.96% (FY2025/9M Dec 2025/9M Dec 2024)
financial_valuation.title: Revenue-mix changes impair comparability of financial performance

financial_valuation.detail: IRDAI EOM regulations cut insurer marketing spend; marketing-fee income fell to nil/minimal in FY2025 and 9M periods, driving a large FY2024 revenue drop.
financial_valuation.evidence: Income from marketing fees fell 88.60% from Rs 3,697.49m (FY2023) to Rs 421.66m (FY2024) then Rs 0.00m (FY2025); proforma marketing fee % of revenue declined from 66.41% (FY2023) to 7.13% (FY2024); revenue from operations fell 81.27% from Rs 4,199.17m (FY2023) to Rs 786.42m (FY2024)
financial_valuation.title: Collapse of marketing-fee income and sharp revenue decline in FY2024

financial_valuation.detail: TIB and TMF incurred losses in prior periods, driven by higher commission payouts; company may need to keep funding them.
financial_valuation.evidence: TIB PBT (91.87)m (9M FY26), (444.86)m (FY2025); TMF PBT 3.84m (9M FY26), (7.41)/(26.31)m (FY2024/2023); Company invested Rs 750.00m (May 6, 2025) and rights issue of 139,584 shares (Apr 29, 2026 resolution)
financial_valuation.title: Subsidiaries TIB and TMF have incurred losses

internal_operational.detail: Success depends on maintaining and growing the network of Digital Partners (including PoSPs). Cost of acquiring and retaining Digital Partners is a dominant cost. PoSPs can self-deactivate via IIB ENVOY portal after a 30-day waiting period, creating attrition risk.
internal_operational.evidence: Cost of acquiring and retaining Digital Partners = 77.45% and 67.50% of total expenses in 9M ended Dec 31, 2025 and Dec 31, 2024, and 69.98%, 66.61%, 69.59% of proforma total expenses in FY2025/2024/2023; Number of Digital Partners 631,885 (Dec 31, 2025); cost Rs 6,825.87 million (9M FY26); deactivated PoSPs 3,639 (9M FY26), 3,845/7,754/7,813 (FY2025/2024/2023)
internal_operational.title: Heavy dependence on Digital Partners; high acquisition/retention cost

internal_operational.detail: Depends on retaining Promoters, KMPs and senior management; high permanent-employee attrition; competition for talent could raise employee costs.
internal_operational.evidence: Employee benefits expense = 24.70% and 39.83% of revenue from operations in 9M Dec 2025/2024, and proforma 33.63%, 49.67%, 48.99% in FY2025/2024/2023; permanent employee attrition 24.24% (9M FY26), 38.54%/48.50%/41.67% (FY2025/2024/2023); former CHRO Shanil Verma resigned effective Sep 20, 2024; KMP/Senior Mgmt attrition Nil
internal_operational.title: Dependence on Promoters, KMP, Senior Management and employees; attrition

internal_operational.detail: Generates majority of revenue from top Insurer Partners; agreements (3-10 years) can be terminated by either party; insurers may develop own tech or become competitors.
internal_operational.evidence: Top 10 Insurer Partners contributed 72.47% and 65.91% of revenue from operations in 9M Dec 2025/2024, and 68.98%, 58.57%, 60.21% of proforma revenue in FY2025/2024/2023; 45 Insurer Partners (28 general, 17 life) as of Dec 31, 2025
internal_operational.title: Dependence on top Insurer Partners; no exclusivity

internal_operational.detail: Insurance broking conducted through TIB, acquired May 8, 2024; concentration of consolidated revenue in TIB.
internal_operational.evidence: TIB = 97.37% and 104.44% of revenue from operations in 9M Dec 2025/2024, and 96.32%, 89.52%, 29.10% of proforma revenue in FY2025/2024/2023; TIB PBT (91.87)/(470.58) million (9M FY26/9M FY25), (444.86)/101.49/80.98 million (FY2025/2024/2023); Company invested Rs 750.00 million in TIB (May 6, 2025 board resolution)
internal_operational.title: Reliance on subsidiary TIB for insurance broking business

internal_operational.detail: Uses technology across sales, risk, claims; exposed to hardware/software failures, cyberattacks, cloud outages. March 2026 UAE/Bahrain data-centre disruption from Middle East conflict interrupted hosted services; SOC 2 Type II certification held.
internal_operational.evidence: Employee cost of technology and product = 4.78% and 8.14% of total expenses in 9M Dec 2025/2024; proforma 7.00%, 9.96%, 5.15% in FY2025/2024/2023
internal_operational.title: Reliance on online platform and technology infrastructure

internal_operational.detail: All premises leasehold (tenure 11 months to 7 years); renewal, relocation, stamp-duty/registration risks.
internal_operational.evidence: Registered and Corporate Office at The ORB Sahar, Andheri East, Mumbai; lease tenure 11 months to 7 years
internal_operational.title: Company does not own Registered/Corporate Office or any premises

strategy_growth.detail: Majority of revenue from general insurance companies, primarily motor insurance; concentration risk from regulatory/market/policy changes (e.g., Motor Vehicles Act, MoRTH third-party premium setting); limited diversification into life.
strategy_growth.evidence: General insurance = 93.27% and 87.20% of revenue in 9M Dec 2025/2024, and proforma 88.21%, 79.35%, 71.07% in FY2025/2024/2023; one general insurer ceased engaging brokers in FY2022, resumed limited business FY2024
strategy_growth.title: Revenue concentration in general (motor) insurance

strategy_growth.detail: Depends on customers, Digital Partners and insurers accepting online insurance distribution; reluctance, especially in lower-tier/rural areas, could constrain growth.
strategy_growth.title: Growth depends on broader internet/mobile adoption for insurance

strategy_growth.detail: May not identify, complete, integrate or realize benefits of acquisitions; Last Decimal asset acquisition led to accelerated depreciation and goodwill impairment.
strategy_growth.evidence: Last Decimal customer contracts acquired at fair value Rs 70.25m (Nov 9, 2022 agreement); goodwill impairment Rs 7.39m in FY2024
strategy_growth.title: Acquisition/strategic-investment integration risk

strategy_growth.detail: Recently launched loans and credit cards (FY2025); mutual funds since FY2021; short operating history, execution and compliance risks; must continually innovate the platform.
strategy_growth.evidence: Loans and credit cards commenced FY2025; mutual funds since FY2021
strategy_growth.title: Limited experience in new financial products; innovation dependence

strategy_growth.detail: Highly competitive market of digital marketplaces, offline intermediaries, D2C channels, banks/NBFCs and large internet/fintech players; competitors may be better capitalized.
strategy_growth.evidence: ~2.7 million PoSPs in the industry (FY2025); Company accounts for ~15.97% (Redseer)
strategy_growth.title: Intense competition in insurance distribution

strategy_growth.detail: Growth depends on retaining/attracting customers and renewals via Digital Partners and enterprise clients; insurers may discontinue products.
strategy_growth.evidence: Insurance policies sold 5.53 million (9M FY26), 6.11/4.75/5.48 million (FY2025/2024/2023); in 9M FY26 one general insurer discontinued a healthcare policy and one life insurer replaced a policy
strategy_growth.title: Retaining and expanding the customer base

Subsidiary (TIB) acquired from a promoter - related-party transaction
Heavily OFS-driven exit for PE/VC investors
strengths_observed: Largest certified PoSP network among peer group; 631,885 Digital Partners (incl. 507,124 PoSPs) as of Dec 31, 2025
Platform Premium CAGR of 33.34% (FY20-FY25), with GDPI growth ~3x the retail insurance market
Deep B30+ (beyond top-30 city) penetration (75.13% of Platform Premium, Dec 31, 2025), aligned with the fastest-growing market segment
45 Insurer Partners (75% of Indian insurers) and asset-light, network-effect model
Marquee institutional backing (Nexus, Peak XV, Jungle, Blume, MassMutual) and experienced independent board

cagrs.segment: Retail insurance market GDPI (health + life new business + motor combined)

sk.drivers: Rising incomes and protection-linked spend (Swiss Re S-curve)|Digital adoption (smartphones, UPI ~65% CAGR)|IRDAI 'Insurance for All by 2047' and regulatory enablement of PoSP/digital onboarding|Low insurance penetration vs peers; B30+ under-penetration
sk.overview: India's insurance distribution market is transforming from fragmented offline agent/broker/bancassurance channels toward tech-enabled 'phygital' brokers using the PoSP model. Rising incomes, digital adoption and IRDAI's 'Insurance for All by 2047' vision underpin growth, especially in B30+ (beyond top-30 city) markets. Industry data sourced from the commissioned Redseer Report (May 2026).
sk.structure: Life, health and motor account for ~92% of GDPI (FY2025). Distribution shifting from offline agents/brokers/bancassurance to tech-enabled digital brokers adopting the PoSP model. B30+ markets (rest of India ex top-30 cities) are 50-60% of premium and expected to grow up to 1.6x faster than T30.

drhp.strategies: Grow Digital Partner network and Active Transacting Partners|Invest in AI/agentic tools to improve partner productivity and service|Expand enterprise (Turtlefin, OneAPI) and cross-sell MF/loans/deposits|Pursue inorganic growth via unidentified acquisitions
